claims.title: gpt-5.6-sol used as a stand-in for tier-1/trivial OpenAI model in review.test.ts
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**gpt-5.6-sol used as a stand-in for tier-1/trivial OpenAI model in review.test.ts**

These `runAgent caching + telemetry` tests build `ModelSelection` objects with `model: "gpt-5.6-sol"` for `tier: 1` and `tier: 3` selections (previously `gpt-5.1`). Per the new `OPENAI_TIER_MAP` in `router.ts`, `gpt-5.6-sol` is only ever selected for the `deep` tier (tier 4), never tier 1 or tier 3. Since these are hand-built `ModelSelection` fixtures rather than values from `routeModel`, the tests still pass, but the model name no longer reflects a routing combination `routeModel` would actually produce, which could mask a routing regression if `runAgent`'s behavior were ever made model-name-dependent for reasoning-effort mapping in the future.

claims.title: gpt-5.6-sol capped at effort "high" previously, now routed to "xhigh" for deep tier without a stated verification note
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**gpt-5.6-sol capped at effort "high" previously, now routed to "xhigh" for deep tier without a stated verification note**

The old OPENAI_TIER_MAP_API_KEY/OAUTH explicitly capped gpt-5.5's deep-tier effort at "high" with a comment stating "xhigh" was unverified on the OpenAI API. The new OPENAI_TIER_MAP silently drops that caveat and sets deep-tier effort to "xhigh" for gpt-5.6-sol with no comment indicating this was confirmed. Given the PR body only claims gpt-5.6-terra was live-verified (not gpt-5.6-sol / xhigh specifically), this could be an unverified assumption carried over from the Anthropic side. If gpt-5.6-sol rejects "xhigh" the same way gpt-5.1 rejected the OAuth backend, this would break every deep-tier OpenAI review immediately (both webhook and watch paths), since there's no fallback here.

**triage.ts oauth-mode comment no longer matches behavior — verify test intent**

The test name says "routes openai triage calls to gpt-5.6-luna under oauth auth too" and correctly expects gpt-5.6-luna, consistent with the unification. This is fine, just noting the test still passes an `auth` object with `mode: "oauth"` purely to exercise the `createAIModel(..., auth)` pass-through — that's appropriate and not a defect, but the surrounding comment above the test (removed in this diff) previously explained why oauth needed separate handling; now that gpt-5.1/gpt-5.4 split is gone, confirm no other code path still branches on auth.mode for openai model selection (e.g., stale conditionals elsewhere in triage.ts or router.ts) since a leftover branch would silently diverge from this test's assumption.

claims.title: gpt-5.6-sol pricing test comment/value mismatch check
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**gpt-5.6-sol pricing test comment/value mismatch check**

In src/models.ts, `gpt-5.6-sol` is priced identically to the old `claude-opus-5`/`gpt-5.5` rate ($5/$30), while `gpt-5.6-terra` is priced at $2/$12 — higher output rate than `claude-sonnet-5`'s $2/$10 despite `router.ts` routing `normal`/`complex` tiers to terra as the 'lower' tier below sol. This isn't a bug per se (pricing doesn't have to track routing tier ordering), but worth a sanity check: `gpt-5.6-luna` at $0.20/$1.20 is far cheaper than `gpt-5.1`'s old $1.25/$10, a >8x drop in output price for what's described as merely a renamed/modernized 'cheapest tier'. If this pricing was estimated rather than confirmed (unlike the PR body's claim that all three tiers were verified against `developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}`), cost telemetry in reports could be significantly wrong.

claims.title: gpt-5.6-sol deep-tier effort raised from "high" to "xhigh" without prior live verification of that exact path via the API-key backend
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**gpt-5.6-sol deep-tier effort raised from "high" to "xhigh" without prior live verification of that exact path via the API-key backend**

The new comment states the API-key backend was down during this change and that xhigh-effort gpt-5.6-sol was only verified against the OAuth backend ("directly against createAIModel") plus vendor docs, not via a live end-to-end run through this exact code path. Since routeModel no longer splits by auth mode, the deep tier for hosted webhook bots and `ai-review audit` (which run on the API-key backend) will now request `effort: "xhigh"` for gpt-5.6-sol without a same-backend live confirmation that xhigh is accepted there. The previous version of this map deliberately kept effort capped at "high" specifically because xhigh support was unconfirmed on the OpenAI API; that caveat has been removed here based on partial verification. If xhigh is rejected by the API-key backend for gpt-5.6-sol, every deep-tier OpenAI review through the hosted bot path will fail outright (not just be more expensive), and the PR's stated verification only covers the OAuth backend.

claims.title: computeCost has no protection against floating-point summation drift for repeated/large usage
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**computeCost has no protection against floating-point summation drift for repeated/large usage**

`computeCost` sums `(promptTokens/1e6)*rate.input + (completionTokens/1e6)*rate.output` and returns the raw float with no rounding. This isn't a new defect introduced by this PR (the function shape is unchanged), but the new TOKEN_RATES values (e.g. `gpt-5.6-luna` at $0.20/$1.20) make small-value floating point drift more visible in cost aggregation across many agent calls. Consider rounding to a fixed number of decimal places (e.g. 6) at the boundary where costs are summed for reporting, to avoid accumulating float error in the persisted report/metadata.

claims.title: TOKEN_RATES has no compile-time link to router model IDs, so a router rename silently zeroes cost
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**TOKEN_RATES has no compile-time link to router model IDs, so a router rename silently zeroes cost**

`TOKEN_RATES` is a plain string-keyed record with no type-level relationship to the model IDs produced by `routeModel` in `src/router.ts` (or `QC_OPENAI_MODEL`/`QC_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` in `src/improve/qc.ts`). Per `computeCost`'s existing behavior (confirmed by `models.test.ts`'s "unknown-model-xyz" case), any model ID not present in this table silently costs $0 rather than erroring or warning. This PR changes model IDs in three places (`router.ts`, `qc.ts`, and `TOKEN_RATES` itself) that must all stay in sync by convention only — a future rename in one location without the corresponding update here would silently zero out cost tracking for that model rather than surfacing as a bug. Consider deriving `TOKEN_RATES`'s keys from a shared union type of router-selectable models, or adding a runtime assertion/warning when `computeCost` is called with a model absent from the table.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 3dde5ee — dropped the `tier` property from the three gpt-5.6-sol fixtures (this one, and the two at what were lines 1135/1158). `ModelSelection` has no `tier` field at all; it was unused, cast-through cruft from before this PR, not a real routing output — so rather than pick a "realistic" tier number that still would not mean anything, I removed it.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in bfd6d4b — live-tested `gpt-5.6-sol` at effort `xhigh` directly against `createAIModel` over the OAuth backend (completes normally, no rejection) and rewrote the comment to state exactly what was live-verified vs. doc-confirmed-only.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Verified — the only remaining `auth.mode` branches in the codebase are in `src/models.ts` `createAIModel()` (lines 44/61), and those are unrelated to this PR's change: they select HTTP transport/auth plumbing (API-key client vs. OAuth client + custom fetch), not which model to call. `routeModel`/`triageSelection` no longer branch on auth mode anywhere — grepped `authMode|auth\.mode` across `src/` outside test files to confirm.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: No code change — the PR body already states these three rates were confirmed against developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna} (Aug 2026), which is also cited directly in the `TOKEN_RATES` comment. luna at $0.20/$1.20 vs gpt-5.1's old $1.25/$10 is a real, large drop, but it reflects GPT-5.6 luna being a genuinely cheaper tier per the vendor's own pricing page, not an estimate.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Confirmed real and not yet resolvable: gpt-5.6-sol at effort xhigh has only been live-verified over the OAuth/subscription backend, not the API-key backend — the API-key backend is down (known outage, documented in this repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, unrelated to this change) so a same-path live run isn't possible right now. This is a deliberate, accepted risk for this PR, not an oversight: the router.ts comment already states precisely this (OAuth-verified + vendor-docs-confirmed only, API-key path pending re-verification once the outage clears). Leaving this thread open rather than resolving it — it needs the repo owner's sign-off to accept, or a decision to add a defensive fallback, neither of which is mine to make unilaterally.
